pointers.sentence: It does four things in order: resolve the path to a view, offer the view to the middleware's `process_view` hooks, call it, and check its result (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response`).

`BaseHandler.resolve_request` asks `get_resolver` for the resolver of the current URLconf, which is `settings.ROOT_URLCONF` unless a middleware has set an attribute named `"urlconf"` on the request (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.resolve_request`).

`get_resolver` is backed by a function wrapped in `functools.cache`, so one `URLResolver` is made for each different value that function is given, and kept ([From a URLconf to a tree](../urls/urlconf.md#the-root-resolver)) (`django/urls/resolvers.py:get_resolver`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:_get_cached_resolver`).

That list is a `cached_property`, `URLResolver.url_patterns`, and reading it for the first time reads another, `URLResolver.urlconf_module`, which imports the URLconf, here `settings.ROOT_URLCONF` (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.url_patterns`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.urlconf_module`).

That list is a `cached_property`, `URLResolver.url_patterns`, and reading it for the first time reads another, `URLResolver.urlconf_module`, which imports the URLconf, here `settings.ROOT_URLCONF` (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.url_patterns`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.urlconf_module`).

`path` and `re_path` are one function, `_path`, with the matcher's class fixed to `RoutePattern` for the first and to `RegexPattern` for the second, so the two make the same objects around a different matcher (`django/urls/conf.py:_path`).

`_route_to_regex` writes each parameter in angle brackets as a named group whose body is its converter's own regular expression, and for a view's pattern it anchors the end (`django/urls/resolvers.py:_route_to_regex`, `django/urls/converters.py:IntConverter`).

`URLResolver.resolve` tries the entries of its list in order and returns at the first match (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.resolve`).
For a `URLPattern` that is `URLPattern.resolve`, which asks its matcher, here a `RoutePattern`, to match what is left of the path (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLPattern.resolve`).
A converter that raises `ValueError` makes the pattern not match (`django/urls/resolvers.py:RoutePattern.match`).
A `ResolverMatch` holds the view, its positional and keyword arguments, the pattern's name, the route, and the namespaces on the way (`django/urls/resolvers.py:ResolverMatch.__init__`).

The `convert_exception_to_response` wrapper around the centre turns it into a 404 response, and, when `settings.DEBUG` is true, into the page that shows the entries tried (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`).

`resolve_request` keeps the match as `HttpRequest.resolver_match`, where the view and anything after it can read which pattern answered, and returns it; `_get_response` unpacks it into the three things it needs, the view, its positional arguments and its keyword arguments (`django/urls/resolvers.py:ResolverMatch.__getitem__`).
With a view in hand, the handler runs the `process_view` hooks in the order of `settings.MIDDLEWARE` (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`).

It passes over a view that `csrf_exempt` has marked, and that mark is why its check waits for `process_view`: `process_request` runs before the path is resolved, and `process_view` is the first kind of hook handed the view ([The centre of the chain](../handlers/view.md#the-process_view-hooks)) (`django/views/decorators/csrf.py:csrf_exempt`).

For any other method it checks the origin if sent, or else on a secure request the referer, and then that the request's token matches the secret, by default from the cookie (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware.process_view`).
No database has the setting by default, and the view is returned unchanged (`django/db/utils.py:ConnectionHandler.configure_settings`, `django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.make_view_atomic`).

An asynchronous view would then be wrapped in `async_to_sync`, which runs it in an event loop on another thread and returns its response, because `_get_response` is synchronous and cannot await it (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response`, `asgiref:asgiref/sync.py:AsyncToSync.__call__`).

A class-based view reaches the same point by another route: `View.as_view` returns a function for the URLconf, and that function makes an instance of the class for each request and dispatches on the method ([`View.as_view` and dispatch](../views/as-view.md)) (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.as_view`).

`BaseHandler.check_response` raises `ValueError` for a view that returned `None`, with the message naming the view, and for a coroutine that was never awaited (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.check_response`).
